trigger: Two sequences given, asked whether one could be the pop order of the other on a stack.
key_idea: Greedily simulate: push each value, and pop eagerly whenever the stack top matches the next expected popped value; if everything can be matched the stack ends empty.
approach: Keep an empty stack and a pointer into popped.
For each value in pushed, push it.
While stack top equals popped[pointer], pop and advance pointer.
Return true if the stack is empty at the end.
gotcha: Popping must be done in a while loop after each push, not just once, or you miss consecutive matches.

trigger: Asked for the k smallest or closest items from an unsorted collection.
key_idea: Compare squared distances (no sqrt needed) and keep a max-heap of size k so the farthest candidate is evicted; the learner used a full min-heap and popped k times, which also works.
approach: Compute squared distance x*x + y*y for each point.
Push (-dist, point) into a heap; if size exceeds k, pop the largest.
Remaining k entries are the answer.
gotcha: Skip the sqrt: it is slow and unnecessary since squared distance preserves ordering.

trigger: Count subarrays whose sum satisfies a divisibility condition.
key_idea: Two prefix sums with the same remainder mod k bound a subarray whose sum is divisible by k, so count pairs of equal remainders using a frequency map.
approach: Init remainder map with {0: 1} and running prefix = 0.
For each number, add to prefix and take prefix % k.
Add the current count of that remainder to the answer.
Increment the remainder's count.
gotcha: Negative sums need normalizing to a non-negative remainder; Python's % already does this but many languages do not.

trigger: Sum or collect BST node values inside a given [low, high] range.
key_idea: Use the BST property to prune: if a node is below low skip its left subtree, if above high skip its right subtree.
approach: Return 0 for a null node.
If node.val < low, recurse only right.
If node.val > high, recurse only left.
Otherwise add node.val and recurse both sides.
gotcha: Traversing the whole tree without pruning is still accepted but misses the point of the BST property.

trigger: Sorted array containing negatives, need the squares back in sorted order.
key_idea: The largest squares are at the two ends of the array, so compare the ends with two pointers and fill the result from the back.
approach: Set left = 0, right = n - 1, result array of size n.
Compare squares at left and right; place the larger at the back position.
Move the pointer whose value was used inward.
Repeat until pointers cross.
gotcha: Comparing raw values instead of absolute values or squares breaks when negatives are present.

trigger: Two sorted, disjoint interval lists and you need their overlaps.
key_idea: The overlap of two intervals is [max(starts), min(ends)]; advance whichever interval ends first since it cannot overlap anything further.
approach: Use pointers i and j into the two lists.
Compute start = max of starts, end = min of ends.
If start <= end, record [start, end].
Advance the pointer whose interval has the smaller end.
gotcha: Intervals are closed, so a single shared point (start == end) still counts as an intersection.

trigger: Count subarrays with exactly k distinct values.
key_idea: Exactly k = atMost(k) - atMost(k-1); the learner's variant keeps two left pointers (farthest and nearest valid) and adds their gap for each right end.
approach: Write helper atMost(k) using a sliding window with a frequency map.
Expand right; shrink left while distinct count exceeds k.
Add window length (r - l + 1) to the count each step.
Return atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1).
gotcha: A single window cannot count exactly-k directly since shrinking can skip valid subarrays; use the atMost difference or three pointers.

trigger: Longest run of a value allowed at most k exceptions or flips.
key_idea: Maintain a window containing at most k zeros; the longest such window is the answer.
approach: Expand right, counting zeros in the window.
While zeros > k, move left forward, decrementing when passing a zero.
Update best with the window length after each step.
gotcha: You never actually flip anything; track the zero count and keep the window valid instead.

trigger: Assign items to two groups of equal size while minimizing total cost.
key_idea: Sort people by (costB - costA); those with the smallest difference benefit most from city B, so send the first half to B and the rest to A.
approach: Build list of [costB - costA, costA, costB].
Sort ascending by the difference.
First n people pay costB, remaining n pay costA.
Return the total.
gotcha: Sending everyone to their cheaper city ignores the equal-split constraint; sort by the difference, not the raw cost.

trigger: Repeatedly take the two largest elements, combine them, and put the result back.
key_idea: A max-heap gives the two heaviest stones in O(log n) each time; simulate until one stone remains.
approach: Negate values and heapify to get a max-heap in Python.
While more than one stone, pop the two largest.
Push their difference if nonzero.
Return the remaining stone or 0.
gotcha: Python only has a min-heap, so forget to negate and you get the smallest stones instead.

trigger: Repeatedly cancel adjacent equal pairs until none remain.
key_idea: A stack naturally handles chains of cancellations: pop when the incoming char matches the top, else push.
approach: Iterate characters of s.
If stack top equals the char, pop it.
Otherwise push the char.
Join the stack into the result.
gotcha: Removing pairs with repeated string scans is O(n^2); the stack handles newly adjacent pairs automatically.

trigger: Count positions where an array differs from its sorted version.
key_idea: Sort a copy and compare index by index; counting sort works since heights are bounded.
approach: Create expected = sorted(heights).
Count indices where heights[i] != expected[i].
Return the count.
gotcha: You must compare against the sorted copy, not sort in place and lose the original.

trigger: Search in an array that first increases then decreases, with a limited number of reads.
key_idea: Binary search three times: first for the peak (compare mid with mid+1), then ascending search on the left, then descending search on the right.
approach: Find peak: if arr[mid] > arr[mid+1] go left, else right.
Binary search target in [0, peak] ascending.
If not found, binary search in [peak, end] with reversed comparisons.
Return the first index found or -1.
gotcha: Search the ascending half first because the problem asks for the minimum index.

trigger: Sort one array according to the order defined by another array.
key_idea: Count occurrences of arr1, emit them in arr2's order, then append leftover values sorted ascending.
approach: Count frequencies of arr1 in a map.
For each value in arr2, output it count times and delete it.
Sort remaining map keys and output them with their counts.
Concatenate the two parts.
gotcha: Leftover elements not in arr2 must be sorted ascending, not left in original order.

trigger: A sequence where each term is a fixed combination of the previous few terms.
key_idea: Bottom-up DP needs only the last three values, so roll three variables instead of an array.
approach: Handle n = 0, 1, 2 directly.
Keep three variables for T(i-3), T(i-2), T(i-1).
Loop from 3 to n, shifting variables and summing.
Return the last variable.
gotcha: Naive recursion is exponential; always memoize or iterate.

trigger: A tree question phrased in terms of levels or depth sums.
key_idea: Level-order BFS sums each level as you go; track the first level whose sum exceeds the current max.
approach: Queue starts with the root at level 1.
Process one whole level at a time, summing values.
If sum > best, record best and this level.
Enqueue children for the next level.
gotcha: Use strict > when updating so ties return the smallest level.

trigger: Repeatedly merge two items where the cost is their sum and you want the minimum total.
key_idea: Always merge the two smallest sticks (Huffman idea) so large sums are added as few times as possible.
approach: Heapify the sticks as a min-heap.
While more than one stick, pop the two smallest.
Add their sum to the cost and push the sum back.
Return the total cost.
gotcha: A single stick costs 0; the loop must not run when only one element remains.

trigger: How many times can a target word be formed from a multiset of letters.
key_idea: Count each letter in text and divide by how many times the word needs it; the minimum ratio limits the count.
approach: Count letters of text that appear in the word.
Divide counts for l and o by 2 since balloon needs two each.
Return the minimum across b, a, l, o, n.
gotcha: Forgetting that l and o appear twice in balloon overcounts the answer.

trigger: Check whether every value's frequency is distinct.
key_idea: Build a frequency map, then compare the number of frequencies to the size of the set of frequencies.
approach: Count each value in a dict.
Put the counts into a set.
Return True if set size equals dict size.
gotcha: Compare the frequencies for uniqueness, not the values themselves.

trigger: Remove groups of k adjacent equal characters repeatedly.
key_idea: Store (count, char) pairs on a stack; increment the top's count on a match and pop when it reaches k, which handles cascades naturally.
approach: For each char, if stack top has same char, increment its count.
Otherwise push [1, char].
If the top's count hits k, pop it.
Rebuild the string by repeating each char by its count.
gotcha: Storing only characters forces repeated k-length checks; storing counts keeps it linear.

trigger: Return top suggestions after each typed prefix of a query.
key_idea: Insert products into a trie, then for each prefix walk to its node and DFS in alphabetical order, stopping after 3 words; sorting plus binary search also works.
approach: Insert every product into a trie.
For each prefix of searchWord, walk the trie to that node.
DFS children in a-z order, collecting words until 3 are found.
If the prefix node is missing, append an empty list.
gotcha: Once a prefix has no match, every longer prefix also has none; results must still be lexicographically smallest.

trigger: Many range queries over an array with an operation that has an inverse.
key_idea: XOR is its own inverse, so prefix XOR lets any range be answered as prefix[r+1] ^ prefix[l].
approach: Build prefix where prefix[i+1] = prefix[i] ^ arr[i].
For each query (l, r) answer prefix[r+1] ^ prefix[l].
Return the list of answers.
gotcha: Off-by-one on prefix indexing; the size n+1 array with prefix[0] = 0 avoids special-casing l = 0.

trigger: Minimum edits to make a string a palindrome.
key_idea: Answer is n minus the longest palindromic subsequence; equivalently dp(l, r) matches ends when equal, else 1 plus the better of dropping one end.
approach: Define dfs(l, r) = min insertions for s[l..r].
If l >= r return 0.
If s[l] == s[r], return dfs(l+1, r-1).
Else return 1 + min(dfs(l+1, r), dfs(l, r-1)).
Memoize on (l, r).
gotcha: Deep recursion may hit Python's limit on long strings; iterate over increasing lengths if needed.

trigger: Make one string an anagram of another with minimum replacements.
key_idea: Count t's letters, subtract s's letters; the sum of positive leftovers is how many characters in t must change.
approach: Count characters of t.
Decrement the count for each character of s.
Sum all positive counts and return.
gotcha: Only sum the positive side; summing absolute differences double-counts.

trigger: Two players alternate taking 1 to 3 items from the front and each plays optimally.
key_idea: Let dp[i] be the best score difference the current player can achieve from index i; take 1, 2, or 3 stones and subtract the opponent's best from the rest.
approach: Define dfs(i) returning best (self - opponent) from i.
Try taking 1, 2, or 3 stones, adding their sum minus dfs(next).
Memoize and return the max.
Compare dfs(0) with 0 to decide Alice, Bob, or Tie.
gotcha: Model the score as a difference, not two separate totals, or the state explodes.

trigger: Check whether an array matches a root-to-leaf path in a tree.
key_idea: DFS carrying an index into arr; fail early on value mismatch, succeed only when a leaf is reached at the last index.
approach: dfs(node, idx): return False if node is null, idx out of range, or value mismatch.
If node is a leaf, return idx == len(arr) - 1.
Return dfs(left, idx+1) or dfs(right, idx+1).
gotcha: Matching a prefix of the array is not enough; the path must end at a leaf exactly when the array ends.

trigger: Longest subarray where max minus min stays within a limit.
key_idea: Maintain two monotonic deques (decreasing for max, increasing for min) so the window's max and min are at their fronts in O(1).
approach: For each right, push into both deques keeping them monotonic.
While maxDeque front - minDeque front > limit, advance left.
Pop from a deque's front if its value equals nums[left] being removed.
Track the max window length.
gotcha: When shrinking, only pop a deque's front if it equals the element leaving the window.

trigger: A node's status depends on the maximum value along its root-to-node path.
key_idea: Pass the running maximum down the DFS; a node is good if its value is at least that max.
approach: Start DFS with (root, root.val).
If node.val >= maxSoFar, count it.
Recurse into children with max(maxSoFar, node.val).
Return the total count.
gotcha: Use >= not >; the root and nodes equal to the path max are good.

trigger: Each output element is the sum of all inputs up to that index.
key_idea: Each running sum is the previous running sum plus the current element.
approach: Set res[0] = nums[0].
For i from 1, res[i] = res[i-1] + nums[i].
Return res.

complexity.space: O(n) or O(1) if in place

gotcha: Recomputing each sum from scratch is O(n^2); reuse the previous total.

trigger: Remove k elements to minimize the number of distinct values remaining.
key_idea: Remove values with the smallest frequencies first, since they cost the fewest removals to eliminate entirely; the learner buckets by frequency to avoid sorting.
approach: Count frequencies.
Sort frequencies ascending (or bucket them).
Subtract frequencies from k while k covers a whole value, decrementing unique count.
Return the remaining unique count.

complexity.time: O(n log n) sorted, O(n) bucketed

gotcha: Stop when k cannot fully remove the next value; partial removal does not reduce uniques.

trigger: Maximize a pairwise expression over points sorted by x within a distance window.
key_idea: Since xi < xj the value becomes (yi - xi) + (yj + xj), so for each j you need the max (yi - xi) among points within k, kept in a monotonic deque.
approach: For each point (x, y), pop deque front while x - front.x > k.
If deque nonempty, update answer with x + y + (front.y - front.x).
Pop from back while back's (y - x) <= current (y - x).
Append the current point.
gotcha: Rewrite the absolute value using the sorted order first; without that the deque key is unclear.

trigger: Count pairs (i, j) with i < j and equal values.
key_idea: When you see a value, every earlier occurrence forms a pair with it, so add the running count before incrementing.
approach: Keep a count map.
For each num, add count[num] to the answer.
Then increment count[num].
gotcha: Add before incrementing, otherwise each element pairs with itself.

trigger: Apply a neighbor-based rule to an array day by day until it stops changing.
key_idea: Each day's changes must be computed from a snapshot of the previous day, and you loop until a full pass makes no change.
approach: Loop while a change occurred in the last pass.
Copy the array as prev.
For each interior index, compare prev neighbors and adjust arr.
Stop when no element changed.
gotcha: Updating in place while reading neighbors corrupts the result; read from the copy.

trigger: Drink bottles, trade empties for full ones, repeat until you cannot trade.
key_idea: Track empties; each round drink all full bottles, convert empties into new full ones with the remainder carried over.
approach: While full bottles > 0, add them to drank and to empties.
New full = empties // numExchange.
empties = empties % numExchange.
Return drank.
gotcha: Forgetting to carry over leftover empties between rounds undercounts.

trigger: Smallest missing positive with O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
key_idea: The answer is in 1..n+1, so place each value v at index v-1 (cyclic sort), then the first index holding the wrong value gives the answer; the learner's set-based version uses O(n) space.
approach: For each i, swap nums[i] to index nums[i]-1 while it is in 1..n and misplaced.
Scan for the first index i where nums[i] != i + 1.
Return i + 1, or n + 1 if all match.
gotcha: Guard the swap against duplicates (nums[i] == nums[nums[i]-1]) or the loop never ends.

trigger: Find the kth missing number in a sorted array of positives.
key_idea: The number of missing values before arr[i] is arr[i] - i - 1, which is monotonic, so binary search for the first index where it reaches k; the answer is low + k.
approach: Binary search on index with missing(i) = arr[i] - i - 1.
If missing(mid) < k, go right; else go left.
Return low + k.
gotcha: The linear scan the learner wrote is fine for small inputs but the missing count formula is the interview answer.

trigger: Remove adjacent characters that are the same letter in opposite cases, repeatedly.
key_idea: Same stack trick as adjacent duplicates: pop when the incoming char is the case-swapped top, else push.
approach: For each char, if stack and top == char.swapcase(), pop.
Otherwise push the char.
Join the stack.
gotcha: Two identical letters of the same case are not a bad pair; only opposite-case matches cancel.

trigger: Smallest set of starting nodes that can reach every node in a DAG.
key_idea: In a DAG, any node with an incoming edge can be reached from its parent, so the answer is exactly the set of nodes with in-degree zero.
approach: Collect every destination node from the edges into a set.
Iterate nodes 0..n-1 and keep those not in the set.
Return that list.
gotcha: No traversal is needed; this only works because the graph is acyclic.

trigger: Split a range at every possible point, keep the smaller side, and maximize total over recursive splits.
key_idea: dp(l, r) tries each split and recurses into the smaller-sum side (either side on tie), adding that side's sum.
approach: Define dfs(left, right) with memoization; single element returns 0.
Iterate split points, tracking left sum and right sum via prefix sums.
Recurse into the smaller side and add its sum; on tie take the better side.
Return the max.
gotcha: On equal sums Alice may choose either half, so take the max of both branches.

trigger: Sum the two diagonals of a square matrix.
key_idea: Primary diagonal is mat[i][i] and secondary is mat[i][n-1-i]; for odd n the center cell is on both and must be subtracted once.
approach: Loop i from 0 to n-1 adding mat[i][i] and mat[i][n-1-i].
If n is odd, subtract mat[n//2][n//2].
Return the sum.
gotcha: Double-counting the center element when n is odd.

trigger: Validate per-level constraints on parity and ordering in a tree.
key_idea: Level-order BFS lets you check each level in isolation: even levels need odd, strictly increasing values; odd levels need even, strictly decreasing values.
approach: BFS one level at a time, tracking the level index.
Set prev to -inf on even levels, +inf on odd levels.
For each node check parity and strict ordering against prev; return False on failure.
Return True after all levels pass.
gotcha: Ordering must be strict; equal adjacent values on a level are invalid.

trigger: Minimize the maximum edge weight along a path in a grid.
key_idea: Dijkstra with the cost of a path defined as the max absolute height difference so far instead of a sum.
approach: Min-heap of (maxDiff, r, c) starting at (0, 0, 0).
Pop; if it is the target return its diff; skip if visited.
For each neighbor push max(diff, |height diff|).
Mark cells visited when popped.
gotcha: Relax with max, not plus; using a sum solves a different problem.

trigger: Sort values by how often they occur, with a tie-breaker.
key_idea: Count frequencies then sort with a composite key (frequency ascending, value descending).
approach: Build a Counter of nums.
Sort nums by key (freq[x], -x).
Return the sorted list.
gotcha: The tie-break is decreasing value, so negate x in the key.

trigger: Find the maximum row sum of a grid.
key_idea: Sum each row and keep the largest.
approach: For each row, compute sum(row).
Track the maximum.
Return it.
gotcha: None really; just do not sum columns by mistake.

trigger: For each element compute the sum of absolute differences to all others in a sorted array.
key_idea: Sorted order removes the absolute value: left part contributes i*nums[i] - leftSum and right part contributes rightSum - (n-i-1)*nums[i].
approach: Build a prefix sum array.
For index i, leftSum = prefix[i], rightSum = total - prefix[i] - nums[i].
result[i] = i*nums[i] - leftSum + rightSum - (n-i-1)*nums[i].
gotcha: Exclude nums[i] itself from rightSum or the formula is off by nums[i].

trigger: Given step-by-step gains, find the peak cumulative value.
key_idea: Running sum of gains gives each altitude; track the max, starting from 0.
approach: Set curr = 0 and best = 0.
For each gain, add to curr and update best.
Return best.
gotcha: Start best at 0, since the starting point at altitude 0 counts.

trigger: Sum the values that appear exactly once.
key_idea: Count occurrences, then add up keys whose count is 1.
approach: Build a Counter of nums.
Sum keys with frequency exactly 1.
Return the sum.
gotcha: Unique means appears once, not distinct; duplicates contribute nothing.
